claim: The finite matrices, output coordinates, synthetic costs, discrete choices and model-boundary controls printed in the visual guide agree with direct exact calculations.
surrogate: Independent construction from the displayed definitions, exact matrix arithmetic, rational row elimination, Gaussian-rational conjugation, finite enumeration and a separate dynamic-programming recurrence.
coefficient_domains: Gaussian rational numbers represented by G
indexing: Zero-based source-to-target matrix entries; column vectors; right-to-left composition; column-major vectorization.
normalization: Unitary four-point Fourier matrix i^(-jk)/2; unnormalized Walsh matrix; complex Euclidean products use adjoints.
pass_interpretation: All recorded finite assertions and false controls agree with the printed instances in their stated arithmetic domains.
failure_interpretation: An assertion failure identifies an inconsistency in this finite construction, checker or displayed instance; it is not automatically a counterexample to the general paper theorem.
timeout_interpretation: The recorded finite run is incomplete; no outcome is inferred.
nonclaims: No universal proof from finite examples.
No fresh execution of the historical SymPy suite.
No numerical QR/SVD or general SVD existence verification.
No CPU or GPU timing measurements.
No certification of drawing coordinates as proof evidence.
No claim that quantization preserves every real-feasible optimum.
No generic complexity or optimality statement beyond the supplied finite/additive model.
resource_caps: Small deterministic finite inputs; the release runner records actual process caps and timeout separately.
